paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus is never caught off guard. He knew where the room would be, He knew who would betray Him, and He knew every one of those friends would scatter. He says the Son of Man "will go just as it is written about Him" (Mark 14:21). Nothing in that upper room slipped out of His hands.

And look at what He does with that knowledge. He takes bread and says, "Take it; this is My body" (Mark 14:22). He takes the cup and says, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many" (Mark 14:24). He knew what was coming, and He gave Himself anyway, for many. Then He makes a promise about drinking the fruit of the vine anew "in the kingdom of God" (Mark 14:25), and that's the kind of hope that keeps my ovens warm.

Now here's the part that gets me, baker. Peter says, "Even if all fall away, I never will" (Mark 14:29), and honestly, I've made promises like that with my WHOLE chest. But Jesus doesn't only name the falling away. He also says, "But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee" (Mark 14:28). So when your promises wobble, remember that Jesus' promises don't, and His plan for you doesn't end where your best intentions do.
